fullPassage: [P01] When a young man commits himself to a woman in the Sacrament of Marriage, he makes a vow to love her regardless of his feelings. What does this mean? As time passes and the trials of life weigh down, the couple may not feel the sentiments of love. Because many people have a wrong understanding of love, they feel ①justified to leave the marriage and look for those same feelings in another person. This makes sense if we ②reduce love to mere feelings. True marital love, however, understands that the commitment ③transcends subjective feelings. The feelings may have been necessary at the beginning of courtship, but if it evolves into true love, feelings become ④foremost. Marriage is about a choice to ⑤commit one’s life to another for their well-being regardless of emotions. [P02] One of the interesting examples of nonverbal communication in impression management is Goffman’s body gloss. In this process, individuals (A) conceal / exhibit behavior designed to cover or gloss over a potentially negative incident and thereby reduce observers’ unfavorable impressions. That is, body gloss frequently involves an actor playing to observers of a particular event. Thus, body gloss is (B) essential / unnecessary when there is no audience to impress. Unlike much of other nonverbal communication, however, this behavior is not necessarily interactive and conscious. Most of us have seen incidents of body gloss and, on occasion, have been actors in such performances, even if we were (C) aware / unaware of it. [C01] Fluorine is a chemical element that is present in the environment. When bones are formed, they do not contain much fluoride, but they ①absorb it from the environment over time. In other words, the older a bone is, the more fluoride it has, so by measuring that amount we can know its ②age. It was found that the Piltdown remains had minimal amounts of fluoride, so it was clear that they had been buried ③recently. The news was sensational, especially in countries such as France and Germany, although, it has to be said, also in Great Britain and the United States, the latter a country where there were scientists who had doubted the English ‘presapiens’. Yet many supporters of Piltdown Man—journalists and palaeontologists—④agreed to acknowledge the evidence provided by the fluoride. It was in 1953 that other analyses revealed that the remains had been dyed to give them an antique appearance and, ⑤worst of all, the teeth of the jaw, which turned out to be from an orangutan, had been filed down to give them a human look. [C02] Experiments are good for testing the effects of ‘treatments’; a treatment being the variable or stimulus that you are ①changing in order to test a differential response. For example, which web page configuration users prefer. This can be done covertly online by simply randomly ②exposing two groups to the two different configurations. If the dependent variable/objective is time on site then you can readily determine which website configuration leads to ③greater engagement. The overt/active lab-based experiment is most suited to studies seeking to determine ④psychological factors (though the lab can be virtual/online) and generally these are the preserve of academic inquiry. A company could employ a lab-based experiment to test differential reactions to two forms of packaging, for example. The problem with the lab experiment is that it tends to ⑤spread a stimulus or effect. People make decisions and buy things in the real, noisy world where various other things influence and distract you.
